changelog: Per-device speed limit and priority enforcement now use a tc clsact/police backend with verified fallback handling.
Router speed test uses a shorter sustained-transfer method, keeps the screen awake, and fixes upload timing.
SQM installation lets the package manager resolve firmware-matched dependencies before optional kernel modules.
Network AdBlock installation runs as an asynchronous router job so long package downloads do not hit the app RPC timeout.
Existing R8 device metadata, live speeds, rename sync, swipe-delete and update notifications are retained.
Router Companion installation self-heals CRLF shell payloads and refuses success unless shell syntax verifies.
Speed limits prefer tc clsact ingress/egress policing and verify that the rules were installed.
Priority policy no longer gets blocked by an unverified limiter save.
Speed-test upload timing excludes connection/TLS setup and the test uses bounded two-stream transfers.
SQM package installation tolerates firmware-specific optional kmod availability.
AdBlock installation exposes an asynchronous job status API instead of holding one long RPC request.
Speed Control uses the verified R9 shared policy backend.
High and Low traffic priority remain synchronized with the Android app.
Policy errors return the real backend failure instead of leaving saved state out of sync.
